title: High frequency of and factors associated with thyroid hormone over-replacement and under-replacement in men and women aged 65 and over
authors: Somwaru LL, Arnold AM, Joshi N, Fried LP, Cappola AR
journal: Journal of Clinical Endocrinology and Metabolism
population: Thyroid hormone users among 3678 community-dwelling US adults aged 65 years or older in the Cardiovascular Health Study with thyroid function tests in 1989 to 1990; none had thyroid cancer
funder: This work was supported by National Institute on Aging Grant K23 AG19161 (to A.R.C.), and contracts N01-HC-85079 through N01-HC-85086, N01-HC-35129, and N01 HC-15103 from the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute.
authorConflicts: The authors have nothing to disclose.
result: 339 of 3678 (9.2%) took a thyroid hormone preparation. Of these, 41.0% had TSH below 0.45 mU/l, 16.2% above 4.5 and 42.8% in the euthyroid range. For every 10 kg lower body weight the odds of low TSH rose by 65% (OR 1.65, 95% CI 1.31 to 2.07); diabetes was associated with low (OR 3.35, 1.46 to 7.65) and high TSH (OR 2.66, 1.14 to 6.21). The authors cite a British study in which physicians failed to adjust the dose in 89% of those with low TSH.
